growth_story.headline: Seychelles grew on tourism and public investment, stalled in a debt crisis, sped up after 2008 reforms, and has not regained its 2019 peak income per person.
growth_story.arc: Income per person in Seychelles grew 4.2 percent a year in 1990–1997, when, the IMF says, public investment in the airport, the port and reclaimed land helped tourism expand. Growth slowed to 0.7 percent a year in 1998–2009, a period the IMF links to shocks, loose public spending, rising debt and foreign-exchange shortages, a sharp fall in public investment after 2004, and a debt default in 2008. After a debt restructuring and a broad reform program that began in 2008, growth rose to 5.1 percent a year in 2010–2017, with the IMF crediting better policy and efficiency more than new capital. In 2018–2025 growth averaged -0.2 percent a year: income per person peaked in 2019, fell 12.5 percent in 2020 when the pandemic struck, and fell again by 9.0 percent in 2022, a drop the sources do not explain. Growth returned from 2023, but in 2025 income per person was still 10.8 percent below its 2019 peak, about where it first was in 2017, and growth over 2016–2025 averaged 1.5 percent a year against 3.2 in the decade before.

threads.title: Public investment builds tourism
threads.text: In the 1990s, sustained public investment helped tourism expand and drew in private investment. After 2004, public investment fell sharply, held back by rising debt and foreign-exchange shortages that ended in a debt default in 2008.
